_readme: Every {{TOKEN}} in src/ is replaced from this file at build time. This is the
'set it once' file site-content.md asks for: a rename or a price change is one
edit here, not a crawl through markup.
PRODUCT was a literal placeholder until Aug 16 2026, then Dogear, then
Vellum as of Aug 17 2026 (owner decision, superseding the Dogear row in
Project-Rascal docs/decisions.md), and is Pocket Chronicle as of Aug 27 2026,
after an attorney confirmed the trademark conflict the row below was worried
about. Three names in eleven days. Dogear was abandoned because the name was
occupied on the App Store, Google Play and the Chrome Web Store by a cluster
of book-tracking apps, and both thedogearapp.com and getdogear.com were
already live -- see seo-plan.md.
Vellum's clearance question was disputed from Aug 18 2026 -- the owner said
it had been checked and was fine; a separate open item said no search had
been run; neither came with a search to point at -- and it closed on Aug 27
2026 when an attorney confirmed a conflict. Vellum by 180g, a live software
trademark in a publishing-adjacent category (book formatting for authors),
is the mark it collided with. The suspicion recorded here was correct and
the name moved.
This is still a token and not a hardcoded string, and the rename is why. The
name itself moved in one edit, on the PRODUCT line below. What did NOT move
in one edit is everything that drew it: the header and footer lockups spelled
Vellum in outlined SVG letterforms, and social/card.mjs and the three Remotion
components render it into pixels. Tokens bought the markup and bought nothing
downstream of it. Pocket Chronicle has not been cleared either -- it is a name
with a conflict removed, not a name with a search behind it.
DOMAIN and ORIGIN were placeholders until Aug 18 2026, when getvellumapp.com
was registered and pointed here, and they moved to pocketchronicle.app on
Aug 27 2026 with the rename. Setting them from empty is what switched on
self-referencing canonicals, absolute OG image URLs, the Organization url,
sitemap.xml and the Pages CNAME -- none of which shipped while the origin was
a guess. All five have been shipping since Aug 18; the Aug 27 move changed
the host in them, not whether they exist.
'Nothing else needs to change' was true of the first move and is NOT true of
this one. It held because SUPPORT_EMAIL is built from DOMAIN and the deploy
reads the CNAME the build emits -- both still true. But getvellumapp.com is
being killed outright with no redirect, so every reference to it anywhere in
this repository is dead weight rather than a fallback, and GitHub Pages will
not serve the new host until the custom domain is changed in repo settings.
A first domain only has to be switched on. A second one has to be switched
on AND the first one taken out.
Buying the domain is not a trademark clearance. That was written here as a
warning on Aug 18 2026 and it stopped being hypothetical nine days later:
getvellumapp.com was registered, the mark was somebody else's, and the name
had to move anyway. A registrar will happily sell you a name somebody else
owns the mark for. Run the search before the domain, not after. If the name
moves again, DOMAIN and ORIGIN move with it, here.
_price_note: The bare numbers are the source and the display strings are derived, so a
price change is still one edit. Added Aug 21 2026 because layout.html's
SoftwareApplication JSON-LD carried a hardcoded "price": "59.99" -- schema.org
wants a number with no currency symbol, so the display token could not be
used there and somebody typed the figure instead. It agreed with PRICE_YEAR
at the time, which is the whole problem with a second copy: it is right
until the day it is silently wrong, in machine-readable data on every page.
_free_photos_note: FREE_PHOTOS is retired as of September 7 2026. There is no free photograph
allowance -- the free tier is the daily question, and everything that needs
storage is membership. No cap was ever built; grep api/src for one and you
will not find it. FREE_SLOTS in api/src/rascal/constants.py is ('question',),
and there is no photo counter, cap or column anywhere in the service. The key
rendered in twelve places across seven pages and every one of them was an
invented number. Do not reintroduce a free-tier quantity the code does not
enforce: there is no value of this key that would be correct.
_trial_note: Was TRIAL_DAYS = 'Fourteen', rendered as 'Fourteen days free'. Replaced
Aug 21 2026 with the trial's own phrasing, because the sharp fact about it
is not its length -- it is that there is no card and therefore nothing to
cancel, and 'two weeks' is the wording the owner-approved app copy uses for
the same screen. Lowercase on purpose: it reads mid-sentence everywhere it
appears, so no page starts a sentence with it.
CTA_APP_SUPPORT: Free on iPhone. The daily question is free forever, and the first {{TRIAL}} are open with no card.
_app_store_note: {{PRODUCT}} shipped on the App Store on September 7 2026. These four keys are
the whole switch: APP_STORE_URL is the only place the store link exists, so a
change of storefront, of app id, or of the slug Apple derives from the app's
name is one edit here and none in markup. Every store CTA on the site resolves
APP_STORE_URL, and check.mjs fails the build if a page links to apps.apple.com
by a literal instead.
APP_STORE_ID is the numeric id inside that URL. Nothing on the site renders it
today -- it is here because the two things that would need it next each need
the number on its own rather than the URL: a Safari smart app banner
(<meta name=apple-itunes-app content="app-id=...">) and any App Store link
built for a non-US storefront. The banner is DELIBERATELY not shipped: Safari
fetches the app's metadata from Apple to draw it, which would falsify the
footer's sentence that the anti-spam check is the only thing this site loads
from anywhere else. That sentence is worth more than the banner. If a future
owner disagrees, the trade is explicit: add the meta tag AND rewrite the
footer line in the same commit.
CTA_APP is the store button's words everywhere except the masthead, which uses
CTA_APP_SHORT because the nav is a single row on desktop and a 320px drawer on
mobile. Both are plain text in the site's own button. The ONE place Apple's
own badge artwork appears is the home hero, as src/assets/app-store-badge.svg
-- see the comment at the top of that file for why it must not be redrawn.
CTA below is unchanged and still points at the daily email, which outlived the
launch it was built to fill: the prompts were never a queue for the app, they
are their own free thing and the app can now be downloaded from the same page.
The store link is the primary action sitewide; the email is the secondary one.
CTA_SUPPORT: One a day, by email. Nothing else.
_cta_note: CTA describes the outcome, which is only honest if the daily email actually
ships. If it doesn't: set CTA to 'Get the daily prompt' and CTA_SUPPORT to
"We'll only ever email you the prompt itself. Nothing else." That is the
whole revert -- both strings live here and nowhere else.
CTA_SUPPORT lost its middle clause on September 7 2026. It used to promise
'a note when it opens and when the price goes live', and both of those
happened that day, so the sentence was describing a future that had already
arrived. Note where else it lands: /terms renders this token as the whole
agreement for the email list, which is why LEGAL_UPDATED moved with it.
_social_note: The five SOCIAL_* profile tokens went away on Aug 21 2026, and so did the
footer column that rendered them. They held the bare platform domains -- a
link labelled Instagram that went to instagram.com is a link to somebody
else's home page wearing our label, which is worse than no link. The note
then said the account existed but its HANDLE did not exist anywhere in this
repository: social-post.mjs addresses its target by the numeric IG_USER_ID
secret, and a published row records a mediaId with no permalink, so nothing
here could be read to produce a profile URL. That is still true of the
posting path, and it is why SOCIAL_INSTAGRAM below is the ONLY source for a
profile URL in this repository -- the poster cannot corroborate it and no
grep will catch it if it is wrong.
SOCIAL_INSTAGRAM arrived with the Pocket Chronicle rename on Aug 27 2026,
supplied by the owner. It has NOT been opened and confirmed from here: an
unauthenticated request to instagram.com returns 200 for a handle that does
not exist, so the check the removal asked for cannot be run by a script and
is owed by a person. One column, one link, and it is the weakest-evidenced
string in this file.
CHECKED September 7 2026, by the owner via Claude, in a browser: the URL
resolves to a real profile -- handle pocketchronicle.app, display name
"Pocket Chronicle", 29 posts, bio describing the daily question. That is
profile content, not a bare 200, so the failure mode this note warned about
does not apply. The debt above is paid; leave the record here rather than
deleting it, so the next person can see what was checked and when.
One thing found in the same check and NOT fixable from this repository: the
profile bio still says "Vellum", the name retired on Aug 27 2026. Same class
of stale string as api/seeds/email_copy.yaml. It is owed an edit in the
Instagram app by a person.
It points at @pocketchronicle.app, the NEW account. The old one,
@getvellum.app, is frozen as of Aug 27 2026 rather than deleted -- its posts
stay up and its captions are never edited, it simply stops receiving new
ones, and the schedule in .github/workflows/social-post.yml is commented out
to make that so. Pointing a renamed site at a feed under the dead name would
be a worse version of the bare platform domain this column was deleted for.
Facebook, X, TikTok and Pinterest still have no accounts and still get no
keys. One key per REAL account -- do not restore a platform that does not
have one. Each SOCIAL_* key also lands in the Organization sameAs that
build.mjs assembles, which is a stronger claim than a footer link a reader
can shrug at: it tells a crawler, in machine-readable terms, that a profile
IS this product. That is the second reason the unopened URL above matters.
_prompt_count_note: Two counts, both checked by scripts/prompts.mjs against the generated
library, which exits non-zero if either drifts. QUESTION_COUNT is new on
Aug 21 2026 and exists because the free tier now serves the daily question
only: the prompts page has to be able to say how many of the published
prompts a free account actually receives without hardcoding the number in
markup. The remainder -- PROMPT_COUNT minus QUESTION_COUNT -- is the
missions, and no page states that difference as its own literal.
_verified_on_note: The competitor-claim re-check date, and NOTHING else. It backs the twenty
/compare/qeepsake, and it moves only when those figures are re-checked.
Corrected from August 17 to August 15 on September 7 2026: every evidence
comment in the repository is dated 2026-08-15, so the published check date
was two days ahead of any source behind it.
It is NOT a date for facts about us. Four sentences on /faq, /promise and
/compare/tinybeans used to render it against our own availability, one of
which ("new on the App Store") was false on that date. Those now say
September 7 2026 in words, because the live listing is the evidence and
needs no re-check date. Never move this token to fix a sentence about us --
it would silently restamp two competitor comparisons nobody re-read.
_legal_updated_note: The last-updated date on /terms and /privacy, and deliberately NOT VERIFIED_ON.
VERIFIED_ON is the competitor-claim check date -- it moves when the Tinybeans
and Qeepsake pages are re-checked quarterly, which has nothing to do with when
the legal pages last changed. One token for both meant a quarterly comparison
sweep silently restamped two documents an App Review reviewer reads as a
notice date, and the terms page says in terms that the date IS the notice.
Move this only when the words on those two pages change. It moved on
September 7 2026 for exactly that reason: the App Store launch rewrote the
waitlist section of /terms into a daily-email section, and CTA_SUPPORT --
which /terms renders verbatim as the agreement -- lost a clause about a
launch that had happened. Two changes to the words a reader is noticed about.
